seoDescription: A daily discovery roundup of open-source AI agent projects across models, agents, memory, skills, plugins, tools, and bots.
body: Today's discovery pass found one useful addition in every OpenAgent category. The theme is clear: agent infrastructure is spreading outward from frameworks into browsers, memory, skills governance, MCP data connectors, observability, edge inference, and voice bots.
| Models | [LiteRT-LM](/models/litert-lm) | Google's open-source edge LLM inference framework |
| Agents | [BrowserOS](/agents/browseros) | Open-source agentic browser for AI-native browsing workflows |
| Memory systems | [OpenLore](/memory-systems/openlore) | Persistent architectural memory for AI coding agents |
| Skills | [SkillHub](/skills/skillhub) | Self-hosted enterprise registry for agent skills |
| Plugins | [MongoDB MCP Server](/plugins/mongodb-mcp-server) | MCP connector for MongoDB databases and Atlas clusters |
| Tools | [OpenLIT](/tools/openlit) | OpenTelemetry-native AI observability and evaluation platform |
| Bots | [Dograh](/bots/dograh) | Self-hosted voice AI platform with visual workflows and telephony |

The most interesting projects are not trying to replace the whole stack. They each own one layer: model runtime, browser surface, architectural memory, skill governance, database tools, observability, or voice workflow execution.

Start by matching each project to one workflow. For BrowserOS, test a real browsing task. For OpenLore, index one repository and inspect whether the memory is useful. For MongoDB MCP Server, use a development database first. For OpenLIT, instrument one agent path before adding dashboards. For Dograh, test handoff and telephony behavior before production calls.
